dossier.public_summary: The 0.565-day dip lines up exactly with the star's spin period and shows a strong brightness wave outside the dips that is as large as the dips themselves. The long duration and perfect alignment also do not match a planet orbit; together this means the signal is most likely stellar variability, not a planet transit.

reasons.why: Large out-of-transit modulation at the same period with amplitude comparable to the dip depth, inconsistent with a transiting planet but consistent with spots/binary ellipsoidal variation on the star.
Dip period is exactly the stellar rotation period (1x) with high-significance variability, pointing to rotational modulation/pulsations rather than an independent orbital period.
